When you successfully use the Row or Sail Skill on a river or lake, you can choose to either use your rolled SL, or the number rolled on your units die. You count as two crewmen towards the minimum number of crew to pilot a river vessel."

"You are fabulously wealthy and are rarely ever short of coin. For the purpose of securing money through your Career, either during play or performing an Income Endeavour, you obtain 1 additional gold crown. You may take this Talent a second time, allowing you to secure 3 additional gold crowns instead."

"You are used to anticipating the needs of others, and yourself. Once per session, you may pull a Trapping required for the current situation from your pockets, as long as it is Encumbrance 0, could feasibly have been bought recently, and does not stretch credulity too far. You can use this Talent more times in the same session by spending Fortune. Whenever you use this ability, you must deduct the cost for the item, representing money you spent earlier. If you have no money, you may not use this Talent."

"You have learned magic through trial and error. Gain one Spell of your choice from any Colour Lore or the Lore of Witchcraft, even if you lack the appropriate Arcane Magic Talent. Further, treat that Spell's Channelling Skill as a Basic Skill. You can memorise an additional such Spell (and treat its Channelling Skill as Basic) for 150 XP; further Spells cost 50 XP more each time. Possession of this Talent may attract the attention of witch hunters, and complicate matters should you wish to join an established magical tradition. You can spend 100 XP to lose this Talent and all associated Spells."
"You can perceive the shifting Winds of Magic that course from the Chaos Gates at the poles of the world. You now have the ability to perceive the Winds of Magic."

"You are as nimble and balanced as a cat. Whenever you fall, it counts as a deliberate fall, allowing you to make an Athletics Test to reduce any Damage incurred. You also gain Advantage on Athletics Tests made while falling."

"You are adept at offering effortless, entirely false justifications for being somewhere you shouldn't be, or doing something you shouldn't be doing. When you are caught, make a Charm Test, Opposed by your target's Cool. If you pass, your preposterous explanation convinces them for one Turn (or minute, depending on the situation) per SL you achieved on the Opposed Test. If you achieved a number of SL greater than your target's Willpower Bonus, they remain convinced until someone else points out the incongruity in your explanation."

"You maintain a secret identity that allows you to appear richer, or perhaps poorer, than you actually are. You can adopt an alternate persona with a Career of your choice for a set period of time (an encounter, a day, an entire adventure) without having to Test to maintain the charade, and during this period you are treated as having the Class and Status of the chosen Career. If you wish, you can even adopt this persona for the purpose of carrying out Banking and Income Endeavours, however, in the case of an Income Endeavour, you must take a Challenging (+0 SL) Earning Test with either Entertain (Acting) or the chosen Career's normal Earning Skill (not the Earning Skill of your actual Career). If you have the Embezzle Talent, you can use Bribery or Evaluate instead if you are embezzling. If the Earning Test fails, the ruse is exposed, with consequences determined by the GM."

Specie.Explanation: "Reiklanders come from the heart of the Empire and are its most numerous people. They tend to be friendly, open, and optimistic, with the confidence that comes from living in the province that gave birth to Sigmar, the Empire's patron god. To outsiders, however, that confidence often appears as arrogance, and Reiklanders have a reputation for meddling in other people's affairs, convinced they know best."

"Dwarfs are tough, resourceful, proud, and honourable. Given their long memories and proud natures, they bear grudges against those who have dishonoured them, even taking on the grievances of their ancestors. They believe their forebears watch over them, nursing bitterness long after death. Whilst it might be hard to win a dwarf's friendship, once given, it is sincere and lasting."

"Halflings are cheerful, sociable, and possessed of enormous appetites in all things. They care more for good food and strong drink than matters of politics or war, and are notorious across the Empire as thieves, poachers, and scoundrels. Halflings regard unattended property as fair game and see little shame in taking advantage of the careless. Most are quick with a joke, quicker with an excuse, and quicker still with someone else's coin. Even so, they are fiercely loyal to their kin, and few are more generous when surrounded by family, friends, and a well-stocked table."

"High elves, who call themselves the Asur, are among the oldest civilisations in the world. Proud, cultured, and intensely disciplined, they use ritual and tradition to keep their soaring emotions in check and provide focus for their complicated intellects. They often seem aloof or arrogant to other species, and still harbour disdain for dwarfs after the terrible War of the Beard. Yet not all Asur are solemn nobles. Some revel in adventure, taking to the seas as mariners, traders, and diplomats."

"Wood elf life is entwined with nature, and their society is intermixed with the spirits of the forest. They are separatists whose arboreal outposts are concealed by misleading illusions. On the rare occasions they venture abroad, it is usually for war, as often with their neighbours as with darker forces, leaving the peoples of the Old World unsure where the allegiance of these fae, capricious elves truly lies."

Career.Explanation: "You use your knowledge of chemistry and concoction to mix and trade all manner of medicines and remedies. Apothecaries specialise in preparing pills, draughts, and salves, substances created to affect the body in some way. While most of these preparations possess medicinal qualities, a skilled apothecary can also craft stimulants, poisons, and other compounds with dubious effects."

"You create machines and constructions both useful and bizarre, and occasionally downright deadly. Engineers design, build, and maintain mechanical devices and structures such as bridges, canals, and fortifications. While most concern themselves with practical engineering, others thrive on invention and discovery, pushing the boundaries of their craft to create ever more fantastical devices."

"You navigate the Empire's convoluted legal systems, defending clients and prosecuting the accused. Lawyers navigate the tangled web of the Empire's laws, where feudal, ecclesiastical, military, mercantile, and civil codes are often contradictory. They provide counsel, draft legislation, negotiate contracts, plead cases for their clients, and debate the finer points of obscure legal precedent."

"You are devoted to the service of your deity, vowing to live dedicated solely to your faith. Nuns and Monks belong to religious orders, usually living within an abbey, convent, or monastery. They rise before dawn for prayer before devoting themselves to whatever labours their patron deity demands."

"With a strong stomach and steady hand, you practise the art of medicine. Physicians diagnose illness, prescribe remedies, and perform surgery. Although the healing arts have ancient roots in elven tradition, the formal science of medicine is still young and not entirely trusted."

"You preach the word of your god, tending to the spiritual needs of the masses. Priests tend to the faithful throughout the Old World. While many serve a single temple, others wander from place to place, ministering to worshippers wherever they are found."

"You dedicate yourself to the pursuit and study of knowledge, wherever that may take you. Scholars devote their lives to the pursuit of knowledge. Some are self-taught autodidacts, funding a lifetime of private study through whatever means they can. More commonly, they belong to great centres of learning."

"Feared and distrusted by ordinary citizens, you are permitted to wield powerful and dangerous magic for the Empire. Wizards wield the Winds of Magic, invisible currents of power perceived only by spellcasters. To practise magic legally in the Empire, humans must follow the Articles of Imperial Magic and join one of the eight Colleges of Magic in Altdorf."

"Charismatic and articulate, you champion your cause and try to change the world. Agitators champion political and religious causes using print, protest, and public speaking. They muster the support of the downtrodden, hoping the masses can force change."

"A skilled craftsperson, you take pride in your work, creating products for sale and commission. Artisans make goods, ranging from everyday necessities sold by bakers and chandlers, to weapons and riverboats crafted by smiths and shipwrights."

"Street-smart, you make a living from the charity of others using persuasion and charm. Beggars live by their wits, the generosity of strangers, and anything they can scavenge from the detritus of civilisation. In towns, they loiter on street corners imploring passersby for alms and food."

"Perceptive and suspicious, you probe deep into the heart of any unsolved mystery to find answers. Most Investigators pursue cases involving stolen property, missing persons, or murder, though some uncover stories for the emerging newssheets or even blackmail criminals."

"Shrewd and numerate, you buy low to sell high, hoping to make your fortune. Merchants trade in commodities such as wool, lumber, stone, and salt, or specialise in craft goods like alcohol, textiles, and pottery."

"You protect civilisation from being overrun by vermin, helped by your trusty canine companion. The Empire's streets are choked with refuse and filth, providing perfect breeding grounds for vermin. Rat Catchers earn their living hunting rats and delving into the Empire's infested sewer systems."

"Ambitious and socially mobile, you are the hardworking glue that holds urban society together. Townsmen are adept at navigating the complex web of commerce, politics, and personalities that make up urban life."

Item.name: Large Townhouse with Gardens and Servants

Career.Explanation: "You are paid to maintain the peace and keep the rabble in line, to keep anarchy and crime at bay. Watchmen are employed by the authorities to patrol the streets and keep the peace, watching for criminals, fires, strange people, and anything else that threatens public order."

"Wise and well-informed, you provide insight and guidance to your employer. Advisers provide counsel to those they serve. Well-versed in the social conditions of their employer's domain, they are privy to confidential and sensitive information, or possess keen political insights."

"You possess an artistic gift, and strive to create works that uplift the soul, or at least pay the bills. Artists use their talents for painting, sculpting, writing, and similar pursuits to create works of fine art."

Item.name: Brush or Chisel or Writing Kit

Career.Explanation: "Your blade is an instrument of justice, bound by long tradition and employed with deadly precision. Duellists fight on behalf of others, settling matters of honour or fighting as surrogates in trials by combat."

Item.name: Sling Bag containing Clothing and 1d10 Bandages

Career.Explanation: "An articulate emissary, you travel far and wide to negotiate favourable pacts and treaties. Experts in negotiation and diplomacy, Envoys serve the interests of the Empire, a noble estate, a foreign power, or a merchant house."

"As the scion of a noble bloodline, you are set apart from the common rabble. Nobles are born to privilege, claiming the blood of highborn ancestors grants them the right to rule, make laws, and dispense justice."

"You serve those with power and status, performing tasks in support of your master or mistress. The great houses of the Old World rely upon Servants to keep them running: cooking meals, cleaning rooms, tending horses, and managing stores."

"You live in the murky world of espionage, uncovering secrets and manipulating others through deception. Spies are brave (or foolhardy) individuals who gather information and uncover secrets for those they serve."

Item.name: Sling Bag containing 2 different sets of Clothing and Hooded Cloak

Career.Explanation: "You oversee a landowner's territory, keeping it in proper order and secure from threats. Wardens are entrusted with the care and stewardship of their employer's lands and property."

Item.name: Bow with 10 Arrows or Hand Weapon

Career.Explanation: "You are trusted by a local ruler to represent the law and administer their lands with a firm hand. Nobles entrust Bailiffs to represent their authority and collect dues from their lands."

"Wise and secretive, you guide your community using ancient magic handed down through generations. Hedge Witches wield ancient magics, most living in rural communities, hiding away in smoky huts or creaking hovels."

"A skilled botanist, you turn the earth's bounty into remedies and other treatments. Herbalists create poultices, salves, and infusions from plants to treat injury and illness, strengthen the body, and occasionally cause harm."

Item.name: Sling Bag containing Assortment of Herbs

Career.Explanation: "You are a tough, independent killer who makes a living trading the fur and flesh of wild creatures. Hunters play an important role in village life, bringing home deer, wildfowl, and other game."

Item.name: Hawk Mews or Kennel of Hunting Dogs

Career.Explanation: "A hewer of stone, you pursue back-breaking work in the darkest depths of the world. Mining is hard work in dark, dangerous tunnels, and those who delve beneath the earth are tough in body and mind."

"You have a talent for divining the future, or for convincing others you can. Most Mystics are perceptive and intuitive, able to read their audience's hopes and fears before giving predictions just vague enough to seem uncanny."
"Intrepid and resourceful, you guide others through the dangerous wilds of the Old World. Maps are rare in the Empire, so local knowledge can mean the difference between life and death."

"You are the salt of the earth, one of the multitude of rural workers who toil to nurture civilisation. Villagers make up most of the Empire's population, and it is their labour that feeds, clothes, and supplies everyone else."

Item.name: Lasso or Sling with 10 Stone Bullets

Career.Explanation: "Ruthless and determined, you pursue your quarry to the bitter end: for justice, money, or both. Bounty Hunters track down fugitives and outlaws for coin. Some are appointed by the authorities to capture or kill their target, while others work for private individuals or organisations. Though a few are dedicated to delivering Verena's justice, most care more for the reward, often finding the 'dead' in 'dead or alive' to be the most convenient route to their fortune. Many Bounty Hunters start as Thief-takers, hired by victims to retrieve stolen goods. As they establish their reputation, they may find permanent work as an agent for a merchant or noble house, guild, or cult. The most successful (or burnt out) may build a company of Bounty Hunters, working as a group to pursue the largest rewards. Most, however, prefer to work alone and keep the bounty for themselves. The life of a Bounty Hunter is one of constant adventure. Their work carries them across the Empire, pursuing fugitives wherever they flee. Many join bands of adventurers, hiring out their skills or negotiating a share of the spoils while following the trail of their quarry."

Item.name: 2 Bolas or Crossbow with 10 Bolts or Lasso

Career.Explanation: "Determined and rugged, you deliver passengers by coach, defying the perils of the Empire's roads. For many travellers, a coach is the only practical way to get from one town to the next. The wild places between teem with beastmen, bandits, and worse, but with a team of fresh horses and a blunderbuss, brave and hardworking Coachmen make travel possible. Most coaches are owned by coaching companies based in the larger cities. They employ Coachmen to drive in all weathers and defend their passengers and property from hazards along the way. Speed is of the essence, which makes Coachmen ruthless and even reckless in forging ahead on the roads. Most Coachmen begin as Postilions, riding the lead horse of the team through wind and rain. From there, they rise through the ranks to Coachman, Coach Master, or even Route Master. Others drive goods wagons, deliver mail, serve noble households, or even work as getaway drivers for criminal gangs. The Empire's roads are perilous, so there is rarely a shortage of work replacing less fortunate Coachmen. The best are always in demand for unusual, dangerous, or illegal jobs, making adventuring a natural extension of their trade."

"From the village green to the grandest theatre, you bring diversion and enjoyment to the people. Entertainers occupy a curious place in society. They are welcomed by the highest and lowest alike, yet are never truly respectable — a life of performance places them outside the normal rules of rank and order. The most common Entertainers are perennial crowd-pleasers like jesters, singers, actors, musicians, acrobats, dancers, and jugglers, but the Old World is also home to stranger and more exotic acts. Some Entertainers perform in a particular theatre or under the patronage of a wealthy patron. Others travel the roads of the Old World in itinerant troupes, performing for local crowds in exchange for coin and lodging. The poorest are little more than beggars, while the most celebrated rub shoulders with counts, princes, and even the Emperor himself. When they are not performing, Entertainers rehearse tirelessly, knowing a poor show can bring a hail of rotten vegetables. The open road, a new village every night, the smell of greasepaint, and the roar of the crowd — life itself is an adventure for an Entertainer."

"Just when you abandoned all hope, your suffering and the righteousness of your god saved you! Flagellants travel the Empire, flogging themselves in penance for their own sins and the sins of others. The vast majority are devout followers of Sigmar, though a rare few dedicate themselves to other gods. Whatever their creed, all believe the End Times are imminent, and only through suffering can they hope to win divine deliverance for the world. Most Flagellants wander in large bands led by a Prophet of Doom who interprets Sigmar's will. They wear little more than rags, chains, and outlandish garments intended to cause discomfort and pain. Some follow armies, whipping themselves into a frenzy as battle is joined and fighting without thought for their own safety. Others wander alone, believing divine inspiration will guide them to the wrongs they must right. Good folk are expected to welcome, feed, and pray with Flagellants, though most fear and disdain them. Flagellants eagerly join any group they believe will earn their god's favour, gladly taking penance upon themselves for the misdeeds of their companions. Playing a Flagellant means embracing unwavering faith and fanatical conviction. Your zeal may make you as much a challenge to your allies as to your enemies, but your fearless devotion and frenzied prowess in combat can prove invaluable. Note: This profile reflects Sigmarite Flagellants, by far the most common in the Empire. If you want to play a self-punishing maniac dedicated to another god, give them the Lore Skill for their deity."

"Swift and sure-footed, nothing stops you delivering your messages on time. Messengers carry important letters, documents, and parcels for those who can afford their services. They work for merchant houses, the military, criminal networks, and anyone else with a need for speed and discretion. Across the Empire, courier companies compete to prove they are the fastest and most reliable, maintaining postal stations with fresh horses ready for their riders. Among the nobility, however, employing a Messenger is considered rather déclassé — a sure sign you cannot afford a herald. Most Messengers take their duties seriously, guarding their deliveries with their lives. In large towns and cities, Runners carry urgent messages through crowded streets, with many settlements holding races to crown their fastest couriers and award lucrative contracts. Dwarf Messengers are renowned for their stamina, if not their speed, relying on their own two feet rather than horses. The messages they carry can contain secrets worth killing for, and a stolen or intercepted dispatch is often the beginning of an adventure. As most Messengers work independently, joining a band of adventurers is straightforward, and their travels provide plenty of opportunities to find work along the way."

"You are a travelling vendor of cheap goods and services, navigating the dangers of the Old World and selling where you will. Pedlars travel from village to village, selling goods and services such as knife sharpening, mending, and tinkering. Most carry cheap wares readily available in larger towns, along with small luxuries such as ribbons and hairpins. Even the most suspicious villagers are usually pleased to see a Pedlar arrive, eager for a little news and the chance to buy a few simple comforts. Many Pedlars also carry messages or act as unofficial town criers, bringing news and gossip to the quietest corners of the Empire in exchange for a meal and a bed. Others prefer the relative safety of a regular market stall, while some make a living along pilgrim routes, selling religious trinkets to the faithful. Always on the move, Pedlars take naturally to the adventuring life in search of new markets and unusual wares. Playing a Pedlar lets you make a living almost anywhere. You are welcome even in villages that mistrust strangers, can earn your keep with a few simple trades, and are rarely far from the latest gossip or a useful local contact."

"With a wary eye and ready weapon, you enforce the law on the Empire's dangerous highways. Roadwardens protect travellers from the bandits, goblins, beastmen, and other dangers that plague the Empire's highways. They also collect the tolls and taxes that fund their patrols, a responsibility that places temptation within easy reach. Honest Roadwardens are respected by those who travel the roads and can expect a warm welcome at the coaching inns along their route. Less scrupulous ones may leave with heavier purses than they arrived. Roadwardens rarely need to seek out adventure — it usually finds them first. A suspicious traveller, a robbery, or rumours of trouble along the road can quickly draw them into an investigation far beyond their usual patrol."

"You hunt witches and those who give succour to forces of darkness — then destroy them by any means necessary. Witch Hunters stalk their quarry armed with silvered blades and a brace of pistols. They roam the Old World hunting unsanctioned magic users and those who would shelter them. Most serve the Cult of Sigmar, although secular Witch Hunters and independent vigilantes also pursue the enemies of civilisation. Exactly who qualifies as a 'Witch' often depends upon the Hunter's own judgement. Few are as feared and respected as a Witch Hunter. They begin as Interrogators, uncovering heresy through investigation and questioning before taking up the hunt themselves. Those who prove their zeal may rise to become Witch Hunter Captains or even Witchfinder Generals, directing others in the eternal war against darkness. Even so, they are not above the law, relying upon the support — or hysteria — of the people to carry out their grim work. A Witch Hunter who overreaches may find themselves facing an angry mob or the judgement of powerful enemies. Witch Hunters travel constantly, following rumours of unsanctioned magic, hearing accusations from frightened villagers, and investigating signs of witchcraft wherever they appear. Some rely on fiery sermons to stir the populace into action, while others prefer patience, discretion, and careful investigation."

"A dashing and fearless rider, you bring speed, versatility, and skill-at-arms to the battlefield. Whether serving as pistoliers, outriders, demilancers, horse archers, or similar troops, Cavalrymen are deployed where they can have the greatest strategic impact. On campaign, that means scouting, raiding, harassing enemy lines, or defending foragers. On the battlefield, they are highly versatile, striking quickly before melting away. For speed of movement, scouting, versatility, and sheer élan, Cavalrymen cannot be rivalled. Swift, lightly-armoured cavalry serve in most armies as well as many mercenary companies and private militias. Bretonnian armies make use of mounted men-at-arms, while wood elf glade riders are some of the most feared light cavalry in the Old World. A Cavalryman may find themselves on the road if a superior orders them to investigate a matter of importance. Alternatively, they may seek leave, buy out their commission, or simply desert. Mercenaries have it easier, often able to leave their regiment by forgoing their wages."

Item.name: Bow with 10 Arrows or Pistol with 10 Shots

Career.Explanation: "Your job is simple: protect your charge and keep undesirables out. If you need to keep something secure, post a Guard. Whether protecting an important person or building, or accompanying an expedition, Guards live and die, quite literally, by how they respond in the rare moments when they must spring into action. Guards are everywhere, from the Imperial Palace to the bouncers outside taverns, ready to throw drunkards into the street. Temple guards defend holy sites and important priests, while grave wardens watch over Morr's gardens by night. Merchants employ Guards to protect valuable cargo, and the wealthy often rely on trusted bodyguards, who can enjoy a lifestyle far beyond their usual status — if their employer is generous enough. Guard duty is not always exciting — most of the time it involves standing around looking formidable and little more. It is little surprise that many Guards prefer protecting expeditions to watching over the same place day after day. Others pursue those who slipped past them, determined to restore both their wounded pride and whatever was stolen."

"Thundering into battle on a heavy charger, you dominate the field, spreading fear amongst your foes. Heavy cavalry are the pre-eminent warriors of the Old World's battlefields. A massed charge is an awe-inspiring sight, but even alone a Knight can be a one-person army. The Empire is home to many knightly orders, including the famed Reiksguard, White Wolves, Knights Panther, and Knights Griffon, each with its own storied history and mighty heroes. Most recruit from the nobility, but there are exceptions where a dedicated, skilled commoner can rise from Squire to Knight. Despite their reputation for honour, Knights are as varied as any other people. Some are noble champions, while others are arrogant bullies who abuse their status and persecute those beneath them. Most Imperial Knights belong to secular orders, bound by a shared code of honour and duty. Others serve in templar orders dedicated to a single deity, while mercenary and disgraced Knights sell their lances to the highest bidder. The elves have their own knightly traditions, including the Asur Silver Helms and the Verdan Lords, the feared knights of the Laurelorn forest. Even the strictest order grants its Knights a degree of independence. Some adventure to fulfil sacred oaths or carry out missions for their order, while others accompany powerful patrons or seek glory in their own name. Playing a Knight lets you combine devastating martial prowess with connections to the higher orders of society."

Item.name: Large Unit of Knights or Several Small Units of Knights

Career.Explanation: "You fight for money, for glory, and for the entertainment of the masses. Pit fighting is a brutal display of athleticism, skill, and courage. Crowds gather to watch and gamble on the fighters battling for glory in the pit. Victory brings coin and acclaim; defeat means broken bones — or death. Either way, the pit bosses profit. Pit fighting is disreputable and bloodthirsty, yet the crowds include everyone from guttersnipes to wealthy merchants and nobles. Tilean gladiators are the most famous, while Marienburg's chain-fighters and Kislev's bear-wrestlers draw eager spectators. Some Pugilists specialise in boxing or wrestling and tour with travelling fairs, challenging anyone to last three minutes in the ring. The pit is a hard master, and many fighters seize any chance to escape the violence and exploitation of the arena. Adventure offers freedom, honest coin, and a chance to prove themselves somewhere other than the fighting pit."

"A strong-arm for hire, you bully, fight, and even kill for coin. Protagonists see themselves as champions of a cause, advancing it through violence or the threat of violence. All too often, that cause is their own purse. If a merchant wants a rival intimidated, a noble wishes to frighten off an unsuitable suitor, or a group of citizens scrape together enough coin to teach a corrupt watchman a lesson, the Protagonist gets the job done. Some Protagonists follow a strict moral code, refusing jobs they believe unjust. Others are little more than hired bullies, happy to brutalise anyone for the right price. The most cunning and capable become professional killers, relying on stealth, deception, and careful planning rather than open violence to eliminate their targets. A Protagonist's career is rarely a long one. Sooner or later, someone stronger, smarter, or simply better paid comes looking for revenge. Many leave their old lives behind by joining an adventuring band to put their talents to more profitable — or more honourable — use."

Item.name: Crossbow with 10 Bolts or Pistol with 10 Shots or 5 Throwing Knives

Career.Explanation: "You are shame incarnate, seeking a worthy death to reclaim your lost honour. When dwarfs suffer an unbearable shame and lose their honour, they swear the Slayer Oath and seek out death in combat to redeem themselves in the eyes of their ancestors. They cover their bodies in tattoos, shave the sides of their heads, dye their remaining hair a brilliant orange, and spike it with animal grease. Unarmoured and axe in hand, they set out into the world seeking a glorious death. Slayers wander the Old World hunting the mightiest foes they can find: trolls, giants, dragons, and worse. The Slayer Oath demands they fight to their utmost ability, never holding back in the hope of defeat. So with every victory they become ever more desperate, forcing them to seek even deadlier foes as their fighting skills improve. Shunned by their fellow dwarfs, shame weighs heavily on every Slayer. Some grow brooding or belligerent, others drown their sorrows in drink, while a few face fate with grim humour. Each had a life before the oath, and is more than a warrior with a death wish. Slayers readily join expeditions and adventuring parties heading into danger, facing down horrors that would send others fleeing. Note: The Slayer Oath is only satisfied by honourable death. Once a dwarf becomes a Slayer, they may never have any other Career."

"You are a professional fighter, trained and disciplined to march with your comrades into battle. By decree of Emperor Magnus the Pious following the Great War Against Chaos, every province of the Empire must maintain a standing State Army. Soldiers are the mainstay of these armies, drilled to fight as part of a larger group with individual skill supplemented by strength in number. Beyond the State Troops are countless militias, mercenary companies, and private armies. Wherever you travel in the Old World, you are never far from a Soldier. Soldiers begin their military life as a Recruit, and those who prove their courage and leadership can rise through the ranks to Sergeant and Officer, commanding troops of their own on the battlefield. Long periods of garrison duty, leave, or special assignments often take Soldiers far from their regiment. Mercenaries enjoy greater freedom, though any Soldier may choose to desert for a more profitable life as an adventurer — if they are prepared to risk the consequences. Playing a Soldier makes you a disciplined and dependable warrior. Used to fighting as part of a team, you can lead from the front and keep your head under pressure. Your profession also provides a reasonable wage, and fellow Soldiers treat you as one of their own."

"You bring holy force to the thick of battle, slaying the enemies of your god with righteous fury. Some cults of the Empire have clerics trained for war. The Warrior Priests of Sigmar are the most common example in the Reikland, and the armies of the Empire are often accompanied by hammer-bearing priests leading soldiers in prayer to their warrior god. Other cults, especially those of Myrmidia and Ulric, maintain Warrior Priests of their own, each with their own beliefs about the proper conduct of war. Warrior Priests tend to the spiritual welfare of armies, keeping morale high and faith unbroken. They begin as Neophytes before rising through the ranks to become Warrior Priests, Priest Sergeants, or even Priest Captains, leading the faithful in both battle and worship. Within the cults of Sigmar, Myrmidia, and Ulric, they can rise through the hierarchy and become important religious figures. Others shun the politics of their cult, roaming the Old World, and may join adventuring parties in pursuit of their god's will. Hunting heretics, spreading faith through martial deeds, or seeking out ancient relics and holy sites are all worthy goals for a Warrior Priest. Playing a Warrior Priest lets you stand at the forefront of battle, inspiring your companions as you smite enemies. You can invoke divine miracles, rally others when hope falters, and command respect from the faithful wherever your travels take you."

"Unscrupulous and charming, you separate fools from their money; thankfully, there is no shortage of fools… A Charlatan builds trust with their victims before selling them something too good to be true. It could be a religious relic, a get-rich-quick scheme, a medicinal remedy, a claim to a gold mine, or anything the mark wants badly enough to suspend their suspicions. Charlatans use charm and clever sales patter to exploit emotions and psychological weaknesses. Even the loftiest citizens can fall prey to a skilled Charlatan. They come in many guises — Swindlers, Con Artists, and other Scoundrels who prey on the gullible. Halfling Charlatans often operate distraction cons in small family groups. Young high elves, slumming it with humans, treat their cons as a game, proving their superiority rather than seeking profit. To avoid suspicion, Charlatans rarely stay in one place for long. Few Swindlers admit to their true calling, preferring to masquerade as almost anyone else. As a result, they can operate wherever there are wealthy dupes willing to part with their coin for little more than a promise. Playing a Charlatan lets you bluff, deceive, and talk your way through almost any situation. Your fellow adventurers may never entirely trust you, but your silver tongue can get them out of — and into — all manner of trouble."

"A shrewd assessor of valuables, you will buy anything, legal or otherwise, and turn it around for a tidy profit. A Fence buys thieves' spoils and sells them, often to buyers unaware the goods are stolen. Some operate as pawnbrokers or importers, using legitimate businesses as a front for their more lucrative trade. They also act as intermediaries — when high-profile items vanish, interested buyers ask a Fence where they might be found. Some work on commission, connecting clients with thieves who can steal to order. While some build a reputation in one place, others remain constantly on the move, trafficking in portable valuables. After all, a painting stolen in Altdorf is much easier to sell in Talabheim. The most successful build networks of dealers and thieves, moving valuable goods through the black market. The life of a Fence is risky, so they are always ready to disappear or skip town. Adventuring suits them well, allowing them to make new contacts, gather information about valuable goods, and stay one step ahead of the authorities. Playing a Fence lets you move comfortably between respectable society and the criminal underworld. You can cultivate valuable contacts, broker illicit deals, and always know someone who can acquire — or dispose of — almost anything."

"You steal from the deceased to line your own pockets, always hoping the dead stay that way. Grave Robbers work under cover of darkness, prying open tombs and digging up Morr's gardens to steal what lies within. Some go further, selling whole bodies — or parts of them — to anatomy scholars and others whose intentions they prefer not to question. Grave robbing is illegal, sacrilegious, and perilously close to necromancy. After years of skulking through graveyards by night, some become Tomb Robbers, venturing into ancient barrows and forgotten ruins. There they risk the wrath of the restless dead in search of fabulous lost riches. The most accomplished become Treasure Hunters, selling their discoveries to wealthy collectors with at least a veneer of respectability. Many Grave Robbers hire out their expertise to antiquarians seeking forgotten tombs, while others embrace the life of an itinerant adventurer to escape unsympathetic authorities. Playing a Grave Robber lets you explore the darkest places of the Old World in search of hidden riches. You are at home in the shadows, comfortable among the criminal underworld, and more than capable of escaping trouble when the dead — or the living — come looking for you."

"Streetwise and mercenary, you help people find illicit goods and services on the seedier side of town. Knaves help people find entertainment or a variety of illegal and immoral services. They descend on out-of-towners looking to indulge themselves, promising to show them the best places and protect them from rip-offs. A Knave knows the liveliest taverns, secret gambling dens, and every other house of vice worth visiting. Many also deal in illicit goods, selling smuggled brandy, herbal intoxicants, and services of ill repute. Knaves live by their wits, juggling countless schemes and cultivating contacts from the underworld to high society. Ringleaders, who oversee the establishments where Knaves gather, can build lucrative criminal empires, introducing wealthy clients to Fences, sheltering gang bosses, and providing discreet services to anyone with enough coin. Life in the towns and cities of the Empire can become dangerous very quickly. Wise Knaves know when to disappear, whether fleeing the authorities or escaping the wrath of a powerful enemy. Joining a band of adventurers is often the safest way to vanish for a while. Playing a Knave lets you navigate the Old World's criminal underworld with ease. You are streetwise and fast-talking, and can track down illicit goods or shady contacts a respectable person would never know existed."

"You prey upon travellers, extracting a toll from the vulnerable and the unsuspecting. Outlaws stalk the roads of the Old World in search of vulnerable travellers and merchant caravans. They lead dangerous, hardscrabble lives, camping in the wild or hiding in remote villages and farmsteads. Many join together in groups for protection and to intimidate their victims. The most cunning and ruthless may unite several gangs beneath a single banner. Such Bandit Kings can terrorise noble and peasant alike, fearing only the beastmen, goblins, and mutants that haunt the Empire's forests. Many Outlaws do not see themselves as criminals, but as ordinary folk driven beyond the law. Some prey only upon greedy nobles and wealthy merchants, protecting the common people in return for food, information, and safe refuge. Wood elf Outlaws see nothing criminal in driving back the humans encroaching upon their forests, doing whatever they believe is necessary to preserve their lands. Outlaws are not all bloodthirsty brigands. Many eventually abandon their old lives to seek fortune as adventurers, though they may need to hide their identity. Playing an Outlaw lets you thrive beyond the reach of civilisation. You know people who live outside the law and how to survive where others would perish. Resourceful, versatile, and tough, there are few situations in which you cannot fend for yourself."

Item.name: Bow with 10 Arrows or Crossbow with 10 Bolts or Shield

Career.Explanation: "You are part of an organised criminal gang, collecting debts and extorting money from the vulnerable. Racketeers make their living through threats, intimidation, and organised extortion. They prey on honest citizens and businesses, demanding payment in exchange for protection or other fraudulent services. Those who refuse, or fall behind on payments, risk seeing their businesses ruined, livelihoods destroyed, or families harmed. Powerful gangs bribe or intimidate the authorities into looking the other way, and are never shy about using violence to keep their enterprises running smoothly. Thugs collect debts of all kinds, especially gambling losses and unpaid loans. As rackets grow larger, Gang Bosses fight rivals for control of streets and districts. The greatest become Crime Lords, whose criminal empires can span entire cities, or even duchies. Life in organised crime is dangerous, and few Racketeers escape it unscathed. Some flee powerful rivals, while others abandon their old lives after one betrayal too many. Adventure offers a chance to disappear, settle old scores, or begin again. Playing a Racketeer lets you command respect through fear. You understand how the criminal underworld operates, know how to deal with dangerous people, and are never afraid to use intimidation — or violence — when diplomacy fails."

"You steal from others in order to make some coin, and you are rather good at it. Thieves steal all manner of wealth and goods from their fellow citizens. From the lowliest Prowler to the wiliest Cat Burglar, they would rather live by their wits and dexterity than waste time on an honest day's work. Most begin by picking pockets or waylaying victims in rat-infested alleyways. More accomplished Thieves avoid confrontation altogether, slipping into homes and businesses to carry off portable valuables. The best spend days or weeks studying their target before striking, infiltrating buildings to learn their layout and planning elaborate heists that can make them legends of the underworld. A Thief's career is a risky one, and sooner or later thir luck runs out. Some flee the authorities after a robbery goes wrong, while others steal something that proves far more valuable — or dangerous — than they ever imagined. Adventure often offers the safest place to disappear for a while. Playing a Thief makes you a very useful recruit to an adventuring party, since many investigations require stealth or a little robbery. Your affinity for the underworld gives you helpful contacts and your skills mean that you can usually liberate some coin wherever your travels take you."

"You strive to master magic on your own terms, heedless of the Empire's laws concerning sorcery. Anyone born with the rare talent to wield magic must, by law, submit to training by the Colleges of Magic. Not everyone accepts that fate. Some hide their powers, others flee before they can be discovered. Such folk are known as Witches. There are many reasons why someone might reject sanctioned magic. Some refuse to submit to authority or reject the Colleges' teachings, clinging instead to older or more eccentric traditions. Others barely understand the nature of their gift and spend years denying or fearing it, risking madness as their powers grow beyond their control. Witches come from every walk of life, for magical talent favours no race or station. Whether benevolent or corrupt, few admit what they are. To the more zealous followers of Sigmar, there is little distinction between a harmless hedge magician and a servant of the Dark Gods — unsanctioned witchcraft is punishable by death. A Witch's life is one of secrecy and constant danger. Some conceal their powers behind an assumed identity, while others join adventuring bands that care more about results than legal niceties. A few eventually submit to the Colleges, but most would rather risk the Witch Hunter's pyre than surrender their freedom. Playing a Witch lets you wield magic beyond the strictures of the Colleges. Free from their rules and obligations, you can pursue your own path while concealing your true nature from those who would fear or condemn you. Every spell carries the risk of discovery, making cunning and discretion as important as magical talent."

"You ply the dangerous waters of the Old World, transporting people, goods, and the latest news. Boats and barges travel the Empire's myriad waterways, carrying goods from the remotest corners of the provinces to towns and cities. These shallow-drafted vessels can travel much further upriver than larger ships, while a vast network of canals extends their reach. On board, experience dictates your role. A Boathand is the dogsbody, still learning the ropes. Boatmen crew merchant barges carrying cargo between markets, either working for themselves or for a larger merchant company. Many also work as ferrymen or rivertaxi operators, carrying passengers across rivers and between settlements. Barge Masters are expert river sailors and have an exhaustive knowledge of their waterways. Boatmen often find themselves caught up in adventures, whether they like it or not. Their vessels allow them to investigate events along the rivers, and even when their travels take them onto dry land, they can leave a trusted Boathand to keep business running. As a Boatman, you are strong, tough, and accustomed to handling yourself in rough weather and rougher dockside taverns. Eventually, you can also provide your party with a mobile base of operations to travel the Empire."

"You pilot ships and boats through the most treacherous waters of the Old World. The Empire's rivers are treacherous, with strong currents, sandbanks, and submerged rocks ready to tear the timbers from a boat's hull. Pilots are expert guides with unrivalled knowledge of their local waterways. For the right price, they take the tiller through the most dangerous stretches of river, where a single mistake can cost a vessel, its cargo, and its crew. Proud Boatmen may resent surrendering command, but the wisest know a Pilot's fee is cheaper than a wreck. Some Pilots specialise in a single notorious stretch of water, while others can guide vessels for hundreds of miles, serving as Navigators. They are especially sought after by merchants carrying valuable cargo, for whom hiring a Pilot is cheap insurance against storms, winter floods, and hidden hazards. The seasonal nature of the work means many Pilots are free to travel wherever their skills are needed. Adventure broadens their knowledge of the waterways and brings them into contact with new rivers, ports, and people. As a Pilot, you are canny and perceptive, with a keen eye and deep local knowledge. You can guide vessels through dangerous waters, find your way where others would become lost, and know the people, places, and hidden hazards that lie along the Empire's waterways."

"Resolute and vigilant, you patrol the riverways in pursuit of lawbreakers and troublemakers. The Empire's waterways are almost as perilous as its roads. River pirates, wreckers, and worse dangers prey upon vessels of every size, so the Imperial River Patrol keeps the major rivers safe for trade and travel. It is a quasi-military force crewing large boats and ships armed for a fight, the largest of which are protected by elite Shipswords. More common are the small patrols that sail the rivers looking for malefactors or innocent crews to sting with spurious spot fines — which may line their own pockets. Other Riverwardens serve ashore in lonely outposts overlooking strategically important stretches of river. A diligent Riverwarden searching vessels and following up leads may stumble across any sort of nefarious plot or sinister cargo. Such discoveries often lead to adventure, whether investigating with the patrol's blessing or accompanying others to protect the Empire's waterways. Playing a Riverwarden combines the skills of a sailor, investigator, and fighter. Boarding suspicious vessels, tracking down smugglers, and defending honest travellers from pirates and monsters are all in a day's work on the Empire's waterways."

"You live with the ups and downs of life by the river, and the many interesting people who pass through. The Empire's great rivers support countless towns and villages whose people make their living from the water. Some Riverwomen fish with rod, spear, or net, others tend eel traps, dredge the riverbed, maintain wharfs, or build and repair boats. Wherever there is water, there is always work to be found. Unlike inland villagers, those who live on great rivers are open and worldly, used to receiving outsiders who trade and restock at the wharfs. News from distant lands often reaches Riverwomen before anyone else. A Riverwoman will feel at home on any stretch of water, and their skills ensure they can drop everything and find work away from home. Adventure makes an exciting change from mending nets, wading in mud, and wrestling fish from the water. Playing a Riverwoman makes you a practical and dependable companion. Whether rowing a boat, finding food, repairing a net, or swapping stories with the locals, you can always earn your keep. Tough, resourceful, and at home on the water, you are well prepared for a life of adventure."

"You live for the open sea, sailing ocean-going vessels into the Sea of Claws and beyond. Sailors crew the warships of the Imperial Navy and the merchant vessels that trade across the seas. Since the secession of Marienburg, the Empire has few major harbours, but ocean-going ships still sail from Hargendorf, Dietershafen, Norden, and Salkalten, as well as travelling the length of the Reik. Nordlanders and Ostlanders joke that Reikland Sailors spend so much time on the river they have forgotten the smell of saltwater. A whole world awaits beyond the Empire: the perilous Sea of Claws, the unfathomable Great Ocean, the Middle Sea, the Black Gulf, and even mysterious Lustria. Long voyages expose Sailors to strange customs, exotic goods, and tales from every corner of the world, making them among the most worldly folk in the Empire. Most begin as Landsmen, scrubbing the decks of their masters' ships, but those who show grit and determination rise to the respected rank of Boatswain, or even Ship's Master, with a vessel and crew of their own to command. Playing a Sailor makes you a hardy and dependable companion. Used to hard work, rough weather, and life aboard a close-knit crew, you can keep your footing where others would fall and put your seamanship to good use wherever your adventures take you."

"You conceal and shift contraband, avoiding taxes and the authorities who would hang you from the yard arm. By avoiding the attentions of excisemen and customs officials, Smugglers help merchants increase their profits, customers pay lower prices, and even the occasional corrupt Riverwarden earns a tidy bonus. Outsmarting the authorities takes experience, ingenuity, and nerve, but Smugglers consider the risks worth taking. Most begin as River Runners, slipping small cargoes through lonely waterways under cover of darkness. As they build their reputation, they move increasingly valuable contraband, cultivate networks of buyers and corrupt officials, and command crews of their own. The most successful become Master Smugglers or even Smuggler Kings, controlling fleets of barges that move illicit cargo across the Empire. Smuggling is a dangerous trade, and even the best-laid plans can quickly unravel. A routine delivery may uncover a sinister conspiracy, lead to a desperate chase through the waterways, or force a Smuggler to disappear until the authorities lose interest. Playing a Smuggler lets you stay one step ahead of the law. You are resourceful, observant, and cool under pressure, with a knack for finding opportunities and always another trick up your sleeve."

"You officially shift cargo for coin, but unofficially, everyone knows the Stevedores rule the dockside. Stevedores are labourers who load and unload vessels at the wharfs they control. The work demands considerable strength, which is why they have a deserved reputation for intimidation and belligerence. Stevedore guilds fiercely protect their monopoly on shifting cargo, giving them the power to slow or even stop trade altogether. They are famous for looking out for one another in the face of adversity, whether dealing with tight-fisted merchants, rival gangs of labourers, or drunken sailors. Stevedores begin as Dockhands, while experienced Foremen organise the gangs and settle guild business, summoning their crews from inns with a blast of a whistle. A Stevedore might work alone in a quiet riverside village or as part of a bustling gang on a busy city dockside. Some gangs are little more than criminal outfits that move just enough legitimate cargo to disguise their other activities. Amid the bustle of the docks there are countless opportunities for adventure. Stevedores encounter strange cargoes, stranger passengers, and all manner of shady characters who can draw them into intrigue. Their work is casual and, provided they remain in good standing with the guild, they are free to come and go as they please. Playing a Stevedore makes you a tough and dependable companion. You can handle yourself in a fight, know how to deal with lowlifes, and may even have a gang of dockside friends on hand when things get rough."

"You lure vessels to run aground and make off with their cargo. Wreckers lay devious traps and display misleading signals to lure unwary vessels onto rocks and sandbanks. Once a boat is wrecked or stranded, they descend to plunder its cargo and, if necessary, deal with any surviving crew. Captains fear the tricks of the Wreckers as much as the river itself, praying to Manann that neither they nor their crew fall victim to such deception. Wreckers begin as humble Cargo Scavengers, looting wrecks left by storms or accidents before graduating to causing disasters themselves. The most ambitious abandon subtlety altogether, becoming River Pirates who seize cargo by force. Those successful enough to survive eventually command crews and barges of their own. Not every Wrecker is wholly without conscience — some spare the lives of their victims or even strike bargains with desperate crews — but all live beyond the law. A Wrecker's schemes often lead to adventure. A stolen cargo may prove more valuable than expected, powerful owners may seek revenge, or a botched raid may force them to flee. Others simply tire of their brutal trade and seek a new life. Playing a Wrecker means you are adept at ambushes, stealth, and intimidation, with the practical cunning to overcome obstacles by guile rather than brute force. Your underworld contacts and willingness to do the dirty work make you an invaluable ally when an adventure strays beyond the law."
